properties.chose: Superseded 2026-10-03 on Anthony's word by dec:the-designs-lineage-is-kept-per-item (fix-program item 13): the saved design becomes one file per item, so serialisation is per item and the whole-design hash is computed on read.
properties.decision: Implement req:the-export-is-serialised-rather-than-socially-enforced in reflow2_check.py (the CI gate), which already reads the committed export, rather than by adding serialisation or refusal to the MCP server.
properties.name: A second exporting commit is caught by the CI gate, not by the server
properties.rationale: Anthony's word, 2026-08-08, when accepting the requirement; the fleet's own framing ('the tool could refuse or serialise') deliberately left the location open. THE GATE IS WHERE THE EVIDENCE ALREADY IS: the lineage chain lives in the committed export document and its prev_content_hash, which is a property of the COMMIT HISTORY rather than of any live server session — so the server would have to be told about git to enforce it, while the gate already reads exactly the artifact in question. IT ALSO MATCHES WHERE THE FAILURE HAPPENS: two exporting commits break the chain at merge time, not at write time, and both projects that hit this hit it in a pull request. A server-side lock would additionally have to survive the case reflow2's own release procedure records, where a fold rewrites history after the exports were made — which no live serialisation can see. NOTE THE HONEST LIMIT: the gate catches it at CI rather than preventing it at authoring time, so a session still learns about the collision late. That is accepted as the cost of putting the check where the data is.
